name: NGEN World Heavyweight Title
notes: The fed's list of its champions of 20 January 2010 seals the WFW World Heavyweight Title for this one; no reign of the 1990s NGEN World Heavyweight Title is carried onto it. Sources disagree: an Empire Pro Wrestling page of 8 March 2011 has Donovan Astros call himself the "uncrowned NGEN World Champion"; this title follows its founder's post of 12 January 2011.
epitaph: Created for Cherry Blossom Chaos, the fed's first pay-per-view, where the WFW World Heavyweight Champion Felix Red, whose own title was to be sealed, met the number one contender Shawn Hart for it. Its founder, in a post of 12 January 2011, says Hart won and became the first NGEN World Heavyweight Champion; he retired from running leagues the day before.

name: NGEN World Tag Titles
notes: The fed's list of its champions of 20 January 2010 says the WFW World Tag Champions, Problem Child and Cameron Cruise, would face a team for the NGEN World Tag Titles and that the WFW tag titles would be sealed.
epitaph: Created for Cherry Blossom Chaos, where the WFW World Tag Champions Cameron Cruise and Problem Child met King Krusher and Striker for the vacant titles. Its founder, in a post of 12 January 2011, says Krusher and Striker won when Striker pinned Cruise after Problem Child screwed Cruise.

name: NGEN North American Title
notes: The fed's list of its champions of 20 January 2010 says the WFW North American Title, last held by Dan Ryan, would be decided by a four-way match and renamed under the NGEN banner, and that the WFW title would be sealed.
epitaph: Created for Cherry Blossom Chaos, where Psycho, HAL, Just 1 Dude and JGX fought a Falls Count Anywhere on the Mall elimination match for the vacant title. Its founder, in a post of 12 January 2011, says HAL won when he pinned Psycho.

name: BAD World Heavyweight Title
notes: The fed's list of its champions of 20 January 2010 says the BAD World Heavyweight Title "will be kept under its current name and defended at the first NGEN PPV"; the fed's own B.A.D. title history post lists Jared Wells' win over Steve Johnson at Unplugged on 31 December 2009 as the latest change before it.
epitaph: Kept under its name when the fed relaunched as NGEN: the fed's list of 20 January 2010 names Jared Wells the BAD World Heavyweight Champion and says he would defend it at the first NGEN pay-per-view. At Cherry Blossom Chaos he kept it against Jesse Ramey, who replaced Steve Johnson, after Wells pinned Ramey when both men were out cold following a Rage Bomb off the top rope.
